# eFlow

> llms.txt for the eFlow repository (embeddedos-org/eFlow).
> Status: PROTOTYPE — host-side interpreter (`eflow/interpreter.py`),
> example flows (`eflow/flows/`), and the flow JSON Schema
> (`schema/eflow-flow.schema.json`) are implemented; target codegen is
> still future work.

eFlow is visual programming and dataflow authoring for EmbeddedOS,
layered on EoStudio and eBuild. It does not live in `eos` today; the
design host for visual authoring is EoStudio, and the build target is
the project shape `ebuild new` produces.

## What eFlow owns

- Visual/dataflow authoring of embedded applications
- Generation into the same project shape `ebuild new` produces
- Round-tripping against EoStudio's editors

## The dataflow model (draft, pre-implementation)

A flow is a JSON document with `nodes` and `edges`. Node `type` is a
dotted capability path `<domain>.<kind>` with domains: `sensor`,
`filter`, `actuator`, `logic`, `net`, `debug` (new domains need a
maintainer's sign-off). Design goals: author embedded behavior visually
(sensor → filter → actuate); generate C sources + build files for the
target (the interpreter is host-side only, for simulation/testing);
the JSON graph is the single source of truth shared by EoStudio's
editors and the CLI compiler. Non-goals: general-purpose visual
language, live reprogramming of deployed devices, replacing C for
tight control loops.

## Repository layout

- `README.md` — what eFlow is and (not) where the code lives
- `docs/dataflow-design.md` — the draft graph model (nodes, edges,
  types, generation contract)
- `docs/review-note-2026-10-07.md` — dated review note on PR #1
- `eflow/interpreter.py` — host-side interpreter: `load()` validates a
  flow (ids, types, ports, edge types, acyclicity), `tick()`/`run_flow()`
  simulate it deterministically
- `eflow/flows/` — example flows (`temp_monitor.json`, `fan_control.json`)
- `schema/eflow-flow.schema.json` — the agent-facing contract for flow
  documents (validate-before-run); `tests/test_flow_schema.py` pins the
  example flows to it
- `tests/test_interpreter.py` — interpreter unit tests

## For agents

eFlow is the greenfield-build candidate in the org's plan: the host
is EoStudio and the output contract is the `ebuild new` project shape.
Agents generating flows MUST validate against
`schema/eflow-flow.schema.json` before emitting; the interpreter's
`load()` is the semantic second layer (unknown types, bad ports, cycles
all raise `FlowError`).
